name: Centro / Plazoleta de los Zocalos
tagline: The colorful, walkable heart of town
description: Guatape's iconic core, where painted zocalos line nearly every facade and the Plazoleta buzzes with cafes, shops, and photo-hunting visitors. It is the most convenient base for walking everywhere, eating out, and soaking up the town's signature color and small-town energy.
bestFor: First-timers and short-stay nomads who want everything on foot
pros: Best concentration of cafes and restaurants
The famous zocalo streets on your doorstep

name: Malecon / Lakefront
tagline: Waterfront strolls, boats, and lake views
description: The reservoir-facing edge of town, where the malecon promenade meets boat docks, seafood and trout spots, and tour operators. This is where lake tours depart and where evenings feel breezy and scenic, though the commercial waterfront draws steady weekend crowds.
bestFor: Water lovers who want boats and lake views nearby
pros: Direct access to boat and island tours
cons: Busy and priced up on weekends

name: El Peñol Monolith Area / Road to the Rock
tagline: Big views and the famous 700-step climb
description: The zone a short ride out of town toward the giant El Peñol monolith, dotted with cabins, glamping, viewpoint restaurants, and lakeside stays. It trades town convenience for space, quiet, and some of the region's most spectacular reservoir panoramas.
bestFor: Nature seekers wanting views and calm over walkability
cons: Need a tuk-tuk or car for town

name: La Culebra / Outskirts Toward Medellin
description: The residential outskirts and approach roads on the Medellin side of Guatape, away from the tourist core. Here you find local life, more affordable long-stay rooms, and a calmer pace, at the cost of a short walk or ride into the color and buzz of the center.
bestFor: Budget nomads and longer stays wanting quiet and value
cons: A walk or ride from the main sights
